rules.rationale: Halides were the strongest negative in the refractive-index source; by the Moss relation low polarizability implies wide experimental gaps.
Chalcogenides scored positively for refractive index; high polarizability and diffuse S/Se/Te p-states narrow measured gaps.
Strong positive source effect on refractive index inverts: pnictide covalency gives small-gap semiconductors and semimetals.
Largest source effect was metalloid dominance; high-n metalloid semiconductors (Si, Ge, Sb, Te) cluster at small gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Source refractive-index effects transfer with reversed sign because high refractive index implies high polarizability and small band gap. Fails if the source signal reflected shared lattice-stability confounders rather than electronic polarizability.

rules.rationale: Halogen-dominated ionic salts have deep halide p valence bands and cation-derived conduction bands, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Oxide O 2p valence bands sit low in energy, so most stoichiometric oxides are wide-gap insulators.
Absence of partially filled d shells removes mid-gap and narrow d bands that collapse measured band gaps.
Light-element compounds have short bonds and large bonding-antibonding splitting, mechanistically favoring wide gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Pure domain prior: ionic, light, transition-metal-free halides and oxides maximize gaps. Fails if the catalog's oxides are dominated by mixed-valence transition-metal oxides whose d bands shrink gaps.

state.lesson: Refractive index and band gap are inversely coupled through polarizability, so the dielectric source's largest, best-supported effects should be transferred with reversed sign rather than copied positively.
state.revision_summary: Replaced the previous direct-sign anion transfer with a Moss-relation inversion (halide positive; chalcogenide, pnictide, metalloid negative), dropped the low-confidence lanthanide and very-high-Z rules, and added a purely mechanistic ionic-insulator counter-skill. Deployed the inverted transfer skill with moderate ridge and decaying semantic mass.
